disposition_mapping.rationale: The council was unanimous that this gate must survive as a discrete, human-confirmed checkpoint (FSP-R-01, FSP-R-10, KB-03). The redesign automates status roll-up and exception surfacing but keeps the confirmation itself an explicit, attestable human act, consistent with hitl_designer's and finance_domain's insistence that 'no exceptions raised' never silently substitutes for a human decision, and with emerging_economy's requirement that heterogeneous, non-system-generated evidence remain acceptable input.

Council consensus (finance_domain, hitl_designer, agentic_architect, accounting_standards, emerging_economy) was to split mechanical adjustment postings from estimation-based entries, automating the former while keeping the latter human-accountable per KB-04/KB-10. The approved adjustment schedule and revenue cut-off evidence remain explicit required inputs (FSP-R-02, FSP-R-06).

By round 2 this merge with FSP-04 was essentially unanimous (finance_domain's original proposal, adopted by agentic_architect, hitl_designer, emerging_economy, accounting_standards, and conceded even by pragmatist) on the operational grounds that intercompany positions involving a foreign entity must be translated before they can be matched and eliminated, which the baseline's reversed sequencing did not reflect. Intercompany balances and transactions remain an explicit input (FSP-R-03) and KB-14's full-elimination requirement is preserved via a named, non-netted exception queue.

Merged with FSP-03 into a single translate-then-eliminate step on the same trial balance object, correcting the baseline's sequencing flaw. Closing and average exchange rates remain an explicit input (FSP-R-04), and translation differences remain a separately tagged, OCI-routable output per KB-07/KB-08, as insisted on by every council member who engaged with this merge.

Mapping is the clearest mechanical, rules-driven function in the chain and was accepted by the full council (with emerging_economy's caution about irregular local chart-of-accounts structures) as an automation target, provided a human owns the mapping table and reviews unmapped-account exceptions. The statement line-item structure remains an explicit required input (FSP-R-05).

FSP-R-11 requires this function survive, and the council agreed drafting cannot be automated away: narrative judgment on policy-change and prior-period-error disclosure remains human-authored (KB-05, KB-06), now with tool-assisted first-pass drafting. The step stays structurally distinct from approval to satisfy FSP-R-08, and the policy-change/error record remains an explicit input (FSP-R-07).

The council decisively rejected maximalist's proposal to fold tie-out into drafting as embedded self-verification; pragmatist, finance_domain, hitl_designer, accounting_standards and emerging_economy all held that an engine checking its own draft is not independent review and would turn management approval into a rubber stamp (KB-02's evidential-trail principle). This step is retained as a distinct pause point, with mechanical footing automated and substantive analytical judgment kept as an assigned human task performed by a reviewer separate from the drafter, and with an explicit transition path for staff whose mechanical workload is reduced.

Unanimously required to survive (FSP-R-09) and remain CFO-owned, separate from the drafting actor (FSP-R-08). Per the shared concession across hitl_designer, finance_domain, accounting_standards, pragmatist and agentic_architect, the disposition strengthens what 'survive' means in substance: the approval package must carry exception logs, tie-out evidence and estimation basis documentation, with a genuine reject/query path, not a polished draft alone.

The council split between treating release as an automatic consequence of approval (maximalist, partly agentic_architect) and treating it as a distinct, separately auditable state (pragmatist, finance_domain, hitl_designer). The synthesis adopts the latter: 'approved but not yet released' is a real state needed for filing-window and board-distribution timing, and a named human confirmation of version identity gates the irrevocable external transmission, even though the transmission mechanics themselves are heavily automated.

steps.description: A close-readiness monitor continuously polls subledger close status and reconciliation status (manually sourced where no system feed exists) and raises an exception list. The GL accountant reviews the exception list and issues the formal, logged confirmation that the trial balance is closed and reconciled. The confirmation remains an explicit human decision and the hard gate that unlocks all downstream work; it is not inferred from 'no exceptions raised.'
steps.name: Confirm trial balance close

steps.description: Mechanical, recurring entries (standard accruals, prepayment releases, recurring deferral and cut-off reclasses) are system-proposed from the approved adjustment schedule and revenue cut-off evidence and posted with exception-only human review. Estimation-based entries (provisions, impairments, NRV write-downs) are explicitly separated, agent-drafted at most, and require a named accountable preparer to document the basis before posting; they are never auto-posted. Revenue cut-off verification remains a distinct, evidenced sub-activity within this step, not folded invisibly into mechanical posting.
steps.name: Post period-end adjustments

steps.description: The foreign subsidiary's trial balance is translated into presentation currency first (closing rate for position, average rate for performance, differences separately tagged for OCI), and intercompany balances and transactions are then matched and eliminated against the translated figures, correcting the baseline's reversed sequencing. Unmatched intercompany items and rate anomalies are routed to the Group accountant as two distinct, labelled exception queues, never force-balanced or netted silently, and the function tolerates heterogeneous evidence (system-generated or manually confirmed) across entities of differing system maturity.
steps.name: Translate and eliminate (consolidation)

steps.description: The consolidated, translated trial balance is mapped to the statement line-item structure using a maintained, version-controlled mapping table. Mapping runs largely automatically; Financial reporting retains ownership of the mapping table itself and reviews flagged exceptions (unmapped or newly-appearing accounts, restructured charts of accounts) before they can reach drafting.
steps.name: Map trial balance to statement line items

steps.description: A drafting tool produces a first-pass statement and note set from mapped data, automatically pulling the accounting policy change and prior-period error record into the relevant disclosures so nothing is silently dropped. Narrative judgment (policy-change characterisation, error disclosure, estimation-uncertainty wording) remains human-authored by Financial reporting. The step remains organisationally and functionally distinct from approval.
inputs: Accounting policy change and prior-period error record
steps.name: Draft primary statements and key notes

steps.description: Mechanical tie-out (footing, cross-referencing to the trial balance and supporting schedules) is automated, but substantive analytical review ('does this fluctuation make sense') remains a genuine, assigned human task performed by a reviewer distinct from the drafting pass, not a residual check on whatever an automated threshold happened to flag. This step is kept as a separate pause point rather than folded into drafting, preserving an independent check before the package reaches approval; where mechanical tie-out effort is reduced, affected staff are transitioned into exception review, estimate support, or local-entity liaison roles rather than silently displaced.
steps.name: Analytical review and tie-out

steps.description: The CFO reviews and approves the financial statements. The approval package must explicitly include tie-out evidence, the exception/escalation log, and estimation entry basis documentation, not a sanitized draft alone, and the review interface must expose a genuine reject/query/escalate path tied to specific flagged items. This actor remains organisationally distinct from whoever performs drafting (TS-05).
steps.name: Management review and approval

steps.description: Packaging and transmission mechanics (portal submission, board-pack distribution, batch/offline fallback where connectivity is unreliable) are substantially automated once CFO approval is captured, but a named human confirms that the artifact being released is byte-for-byte the version that was approved before external transmission executes. This remains a visible, separately timed step so that 'approved but not yet released' is an auditable state, e.g. where filing windows or board timing require a gap.
steps.name: Release / submission
